notes: Prop board announced three backup QBs before any news read: Malik Willis priced for MIA passing yards (explains SF -1000), and BOTH SEA@ARI quarterbacks (Brissett, Lock) carry heavy Under 1.5 passing-TD prices on the board's lowest total.
Early window punished chalk: favorites went 2-2, with BAL (77.8%) falling to NO and CHI to MIN. One window is noise, but it is the exact pattern the calibration table exists to count.
Kirk Cousins (LV) and rookie Jaxson Dart (NYG) also priced as low-output starters; WSH@DAL is the lone shootout-priced game (Dak Over 1.5 TDs, highest total ~54).
LAC drifted -300 to -310 over the afternoon; no other meaningful line moves on the remaining slate.

Injury-report update (post-read, pre-kickoff): Sam Darnold OUT for SEA and Carson Beck OUT for ARI — hard confirmation of the double-backup-QB signal behind the Under 44.5 lean. Chris Jones (KC DT) is Questionable, which cuts AGAINST the KC -6.5 lean; recorded, lean stands as priced.

MNF read (Sep 21): LAR -310 / -7 / total 47.5. LAR's receiving corps is impaired (Puka Nacua Questionable, Jordan Whittington Doubtful) and safety Kamren Kinchens is OUT; NYG's Deonte Banks (CB) is Questionable. The market itself prices a constrained LAR passing game — TE Colby Parkinson Over 2.5 receptions at 61%. Also on the record: my KC -6.5 lean lost by the hook last night on the same 'weak road QB gets blown out' shape, while the impaired-offense mechanism (SEA@ARI under) won.

leans.why: Two backup QBs compound: both offenses shorten, both coaches run clock. Market already has this lowest on the board, but the double-backup signal plus a defensive early-window day tilts the total further under.

Market prices KC -6.5 as a coin flip (48.1%). A Daniel Jones-led road offense (his own Under 1.5 TDs at -225) in a prime-time spot against a rested home favorite tends to lose by a score, not a field goal. I put this above 50%.

The favorite's ceiling is what covers 7+, and LAR's ceiling is capped tonight: WR1 Questionable, WR3 Doubtful, with the market already pricing a dump-off passing game. LAR wins, but a rookie getting a touchdown-plus with garbage time available is the bet the number undersells at 54.3%.

notes: TNF ATL @ GB: GB -245 (68.1% de-vigged), down from -330 (73.7%) at first sighting. The move is toward ATL.

ATL's two listed QBs are Out: Cooper Rush (the season pass-attempt leader, i.e. the weeks 1-2 starter) and Jack Strand. FanDuel prices Michael Penix Jr. as the passer (1+ passing TD at 68%). Penix's career line per ESPN: 14 games, 59.6%, 7.2 Y/A, 12 TD / 6 INT, 85.8 rating. That reads as a lateral-or-better change from Rush, which fits the line moving toward ATL rather than away.

Sims (v6, no QB dock before week 5) make GB 63%, projecting GB 24-20. The market's 68% sits between the old price and the sims; with the QB swap already priced, no gap is left that the news doesn't explain.
Weather at Lambeau: 61F, wind 4, no rain. No totals press. The total is priced near 43.5 (Over 47.6%).

GB is without WR Jayden Reed and OT Zach Bako-Bewele and G Aaron Banks (all Out per the ESPN injury report). Bijan Robinson anytime TD is priced at 59% (vig still in), the board's top TD scorer tonight.
Inactives: this read uses the ESPN injury report as of 7:30 PM ET; the official inactive list was not separately confirmed. No lean tonight: the market is doing the work.

TEN @ NYG: the week's biggest line move. NYG went from 67.8% at first sighting to 55.8% now. ESPN reports Jaxson Dart is scheduled for left knee surgery and the Giants have set their game plan with Jameis Winston. Winston per ESPN: 2024, 12 games, 61.1%, 7.2 Y/A, 13 TD / 12 INT; 2026, one appearance, 11 of 27 for 111. The sims have no QB-change dock before week 5 (early docks graded worse in the backtest), so their NYG 66% is the pre-news number. Applying the standard 4-point dock puts them near 55%, right on the market. Gap explained; no lean. Wind 16 gusting 35 with 45% rain: the 37.5 total is the board's lowest.

SEA @ WSH: Jayden Daniels is Out (ESPN injury report) and ESPN reports Sam Darnold returns for SEA. SEA moved from 70.0% to 77.6%; the sims already had SEA at 77% before either change. Nothing left to bet.

KC @ MIA: the largest disagreement on the board. The market has KC 83% (−10.5); the sims have KC 56%, winning by about 2. The only material news is MIA's leading receiver Caleb Douglas Out (ESPN). That does not explain a 27-point gap, and the backtest says the closing line wins these arguments. No lean.

CIN @ PIT: the one Upset watch call (PIT +144; sims 53% vs market 39%). PIT is without RB Rico Dowdle (Out), with Jaylen Warren Questionable; wind 13 gusting 21. This call type's backtest record is dogs winning 40% against 40% implied, so it's a live underdog, not a lock.
Other moves: JAX 54.3% to 59.1% and BAL 57.9% to 61.3% (Rio) with no matching injury news on the board. PHI @ CHI (Monday) gap is explained: ESPN reports Caleb Williams faces a 3-4 week timeline.
No leans today. Every large sims-vs-market gap has a news explanation or no edge behind it. The noon refresh re-checks inactives (ESPN: 'Puka Nacua uncertain, Sam Darnold a go').

Inactives check (12:13 PM ET): the QBs ruled out are all backups (MIA Brady Cook, SEA Jalen Milroe, LAC DJ Uiagalelei, NE Behren Morton, CAR Haynes King), so no starter change beyond what's noted above. ESPN: Jets without WR Adonai Mitchell (finger) vs. Lions. LAR's Puka Nacua is still Doubtful for SNF. Prices barely moved since 11 AM (NYG 55.8% to 56.3%). No leans; nothing re-priced.

MNF read (Sep 28, 7 PM ET): PHI −198 (63.9%, unchanged from first sighting), CHI +3.5 at even money, total 43.5. Caleb Williams is Out; ESPN reports Tyson Bagent is set to return from injury for CHI. Bagent's career line per ESPN: 13 games, 65.8%, 6.1 Y/A, 3 TD / 6 INT, 73.1 rating. That's below the veteran-backup standard (6.5+ Y/A over dozens of starts), so the market's discount looks earned, not too harsh. FanDuel posts passing props for Jalen Hurts but none for CHI's quarterback, a sign the book is still pricing uncertainty at the position. The sims (no QB dock before week 5) make CHI 57%; the standard 4-point dock would move them to about 45%, still short of the market's 36%, but that remaining gap is exactly the kind the backtest says the market wins. PHI is without WR Hollywood Brown and TE Dallas Goedert (Out); ESPN reports Jonathan Greenard debuts. The sims' totals ran badly this week (four games over 60 against ~45 projected), so no total lean here. No lean.
TNF PIT @ CLE (7:13 PM ET board): PIT −148 (57.4%), up from 55.1% at first sighting. Spread PIT −2.5/−3; the total eased from 38.5 to 38.

The sims (v7) are anchored to FanDuel's own line. With key-number margins, a 2.5-to-3-point favorite wins about 58-59%, so the moneyline sits within rounding of its own spread. No real gap. The old scores-only model calls it 50/50, but its disagreements haven't beaten the market historically.

Injury report as of this firing (ESPN): PIT without RB Rico Dowdle and RB Eli Heidenreich, both Out, which leaves Jaylen Warren as the clear lead back (FanDuel: 105.5 rush+rec yards, TD +105). PIT's listed QB Outs (Will Howard, Drew Allar) are backups; Rodgers is priced to start. CLE's QB Out is backup Taylen Green; Watson starts. CLE is without G Teven Jenkins and LB Justin Jefferson.

Secondary news: ESPN reports the Steelers traded CB Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys. That's a coverage downgrade for PIT relevant to CLE's receivers (Denzel Boston's 37.5 receiving line; his three games: 59, 95, 41 yards) and to Watson's 185.5 passing line (his games: 205, 238, 144). Three games is a small sample, and FanDuel sees the same numbers.
Kickoff weather in Cleveland per Open-Meteo this morning: high 70s, wind about 12 mph gusting low-to-mid 20s, little rain. Not enough to move a 38 total on its own.
No lean. Nothing here disagrees with the price by enough to grade.

ARI @ NYG had the week's biggest swing. NYG were a 55.5% favorite at first sighting; now ARI are favored at −138 (55.8%). FanDuel's passing props list Jameis Winston for NYG. ESPN reported last week that Jaxson Dart is having knee surgery, and on Oct 3 it wrote that Winston 'has time to prove he's the New York Giants' starter.' Winston's 2026 line is 2 games, 51.0%, 4.7 yards per pass, 0 TD / 1 INT, which is too small a sample to mean much. His career line is a real starter's: 110 games, 60.9%, 7.6 yards per pass. ARI's Jacoby Brissett: 2026, 3 games, 70.1%, 5.6 yards per pass.

The Upset watch flag on NYG should be discounted. It comes from the old model's 60%, which was built mostly on Dart's starts. Dart isn't on this week's injury report, so the flag's hurt-QB check couldn't see he's out. Winston is a real starter, so this isn't a fade either. No lean.

GB @ TB: GB moved from 50.9% to 58.6% (−156) with Baker Mayfield Out. ESPN says his return 'hinges on when QB can grip football.' The only TB passer FanDuel lists is Jalon Daniels, whose whole career is one game: 0 of 3 with 1 INT. That is about as raw as a backup gets. The line moved roughly three points for losing a starter to an untested passer, which looks light to me. GB are missing Micah Parsons, and the sims (GB 21–18) follow the market. The old model's 52% for TB doesn't know about the QB, and the Upset watch call on TB logged this morning stands for grading. Small lean GB.

NYJ @ CHI: Caleb Williams is Out, and the props list Tyson Bagent. Bagent's career: 13 games, mostly in relief; 65.8%, 6.1 yards per pass, 3 TD / 6 INT on 158 throws. That's below the bar where I'd call the dock too harsh. CHI slipped only from 63.0% to 61.5%, and the old model's 75% ignores the QB. No lean.

DET @ CAR moved hard toward DET, from 55.8% at first sighting to 64.6% (−205). ESPN: 'Panthers put Legette on IR; Coker also likely out vs. Lions.' Losing two receivers explains some of it; nine points is a lot for two WRs, so the market may know more. Bryce Young still has passing props. BUF went from 69.5% to 74.0%, with NE CB Christian Gonzalez and DT Christian Barmore Out. No leans. 1 PM inactives are posting now (ESPN 9:51 AM: 'DeVonta, Price out; McConkey, Coker questionable'); the noon refresh re-checks them.

Inactives check, 12:10 PM ET (Oct 4). PHI RT Lane Johnson is a surprise inactive; ESPN: 'Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson is inactive for Sunday's game against the Rams for personal reasons.' LAR was still −184 (62.2%) at 12:10, unchanged from 11:12, so FanDuel hadn't moved on it yet. PHI was already without DeVonta Smith, Hollywood Brown and Dallas Goedert. No added lean: a lineman is hard to price, and LAR already leads 23–20 in the sims. SEA put RB Jadarian Price on IR (NFL.com), with Zach Charbonnet already Out. The board shows no SEA rushing prop yet, so it can't say who takes those carries. GB has drifted from −156 to −146 (58.6% to 57.1%), against this morning's GB lean; that lean stands as recorded. In London, WSH lost Marcus Mariota mid-game to rookie Athan Kaliakmanis (ESPN). Nothing pending rides on that game.

Weekly review (Oct 6): GB ML won (GB 17–14), but it did not beat the close. It was recorded at −156 (58.6%); the last pregame sighting was −146 (57.1%, Oct 4 12:10 PM ET), so the price moved 1.5 points away from the lean. The result is a win; the process number says the market didn't agree. The week's sim grading by version (16 games each): the market-anchored v7 Brier 0.221 (margin miss 7.5) vs the old results model v6 0.207 (6.7). One week is a small sample against v7's 2019–2026 backtest, but the sims graded worse than the old model this week.

leans.why: TB's only listed passer is Jalon Daniels (career: 1 game, 0/3, 1 INT). The ~8-point move from 50.9% looks light for a starter-to-raw-backup swap, even with Micah Parsons out for GB.

notes: MNF ATL @ NO (7:10 PM ET board): NO −116 (51.5%), down from −190 (63.0%) at first sighting. That's an 11.5-point slide toward ATL, the second-biggest move of the week.

The defense explains most of it. On Oct 3 ESPN reported that 'Saints linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf) and edge rushers Carl Granderson (ankle) and Anfernee Jennings (knee) have been ruled out.' Tonight's injury report also lists NO without TE Noah Fant, CB Decamerion Richardson and DT Christen Miller. NO's QB Out is backup Zach Wilson; Tyler Shough starts (FanDuel: 258.5 passing yards, 1.5 TDs). Shough's career: 14 games, 68.0%, 7.2 yards per pass, 18 TD / 9 INT.

ATL starts Michael Penix Jr., with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand both Out again. Penix's career: 15 games, 60.3%, 7.4 yards per pass, 13 TD / 7 INT. FanDuel has him at 224.5 yards with under 1.5 TDs favored. That's a real starter's record, so he isn't a backup to fade. ATL is also without LB Jared Ivey and OT Ethan Onianwa.

The sims (v7) follow FanDuel's own line: 24–24, NO 49.2%, total 47.5, indoors. The old model says NO 54.7% (23–22), and it can't see the three pass rushers. NFL.com has posted the MNF inactives, but the board pulls only its headline; the injury report above is what's confirmed here. Both RBs, Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller, have props, so neither is out.
No lean. The move follows real news on NO's pass rush, and nothing here disagrees with the price by enough to grade.

TNF TB @ DAL (7:12 PM ET board): DAL −460 (79.1%), a touch off −500 (80.2%) at first sighting. The sims (v7, anchored to FanDuel's own −8 spread and 49 total) project DAL 28–20 and give DAL 75.1% to win. That's 4 points under the moneyline, so the ML costs more than the spread implies; the board's win-price tag flags it. That gap hasn't been tested as an edge, so it's context, not a lean.

TB's QB: Baker Mayfield is Out again, and Jalon Daniels has the passing props (182.5 yards, under 1.5 TDs at 68%). His whole career is 2 games: 19 of 30, 4.9 yards per pass, 1 TD / 3 INT. That's a raw backup, though 30 throws is too few to judge. FanDuel priced the downgrade a week ago; the old model takes another 4 points off TB for it and lands in the same place, 28–20.

DAL news (ESPN): 'Cowboys activate Pro Bowl LG Tyler Smith (thumb) from IR,' and 'Joey Porter Jr. was ruled out of Thursday night's game ... because of an illness.' The injury report also has DAL without LBs DeMarvion Overshown and James Houston and CB Cobie Durant. That's three DAL defensive backs/linebackers out, against a QB FanDuel already prices low.
Indoors (retractable roof). No lean: nothing here disagrees with the price by enough to grade.
